headline: AMAROQ NALUNAQ: PEAK 132.5 g/t Au UNDERGROUND — Average 42.8 g/t Across Level 500; 3,103m in 30 Holes Still Pending Assay (TSX:AMRQ)
snippet: Amaroq Minerals (TSX: AMRQ) released underground drill results from its operating Nalunaq Gold Mine in southern Greenland, with 16 of 37 assayed holes grading above 30 g/t Au and peak intercepts of 132.5 g/t Au over 0.50m and 132.0 g/t Au over 0.50m from the Main Vein on Level 500 — confirming exceptional narrow-vein grade continuity. The resource definition program averaged 42.8 g/t Au across assayed holes with 3,102.9m across 30 additional Level 500 holes still pending assay, pointing to a material addition to the underground resource base.

headline: FURY GOLD FORCE-EVACUATED — Quebec Wildfire Halts Drill Program Days After Best-Ever 7.01 g/t Over 21m at Eau Claire (TSX:FURY)
snippet: Fury Gold Mines (TSX: FURY) evacuated all personnel from its Eau Claire camp in Quebec's James Bay region after a nearby wildfire forced a precautionary shutdown, suspending the Phase 2 diamond drill program that had just mobilised a third rig following its best-ever result — hole 26EC-115 returning 7.01 g/t Au over 21.0m including 10.27 g/t Au over 11.0m. No injuries were reported; the company does not currently expect a material impact to the drill program but cannot confirm a return timeline while the fire remains active.

headline: EKATI DIAMOND MINE DEAD — Zero Bids, 360 Jobs Gone; Canada's NWT Icon Enters Receivership After 27 Years; Wind-Down Begins
snippet: Canada's Ekati Diamond Mine in the Northwest Territories entered PricewaterhouseCoopers-managed receivership after 140 contacted parties failed to produce a single compliant acquisition bid by the July 10 deadline — ending what had been a planned 2029 closure and triggering an immediate wind-down that will eliminate approximately 360 jobs. Reclamation costs will be funded by $325M in existing surety bonds and trust funds, with the NWT government managing the roughly five-week site shutdown process.

headline: MAKO SAN ALBINO SETS Q2 RECORDS — 14,610 oz Sold, ~US$63M Revenue, US$112M Cash; Adds 3,000-Ha Adjacent Concession in Nicaragua (TSXV:MKO)
snippet: Mako Mining (TSX-V: MKO) posted record quarterly gold sales of 14,610 oz from its San Albino mine in Nicaragua — 53,120 tonnes milled at 7.54 g/t Au and 80.7% recovery — generating approximately US$63M in revenue and building a cash and securities balance to US$112M at quarter-end. The company also secured the adjacent 3,000-hectare Eureka concession, expanding its Nicaraguan land package to 254 km² and positioning for future satellite mine development.

headline: ALTIUS -14% AFTER C$181.5M BOUGHT DEAL — Royalty Giant Prices 3M Shares at C$60.50; Premium Dilution Shock Hits Record Stock (TSX:ALS)
snippet: Altius Minerals priced a C$181.5M bought deal at C$60.50 per share — a 8.4% discount to its prior-day record close of C$66.04 — with National Bank Financial, Scotia Capital, and TD Securities as co-bookrunners, sending the stock down 13-14% on the news. Proceeds will strengthen the balance sheet following several 2026 royalty acquisitions, with closing expected around July 21; the selloff illustrates how even top-quality royalty names face sharp corrections when dilutive capital markets transactions hit a stretched tape.

headline: SCORPIO GOLDWEDGE: 2.05 g/t Au OVER 97.99m IN WALKER LANE — Sub-Intervals Hit 18.19 g/t and 11.41 g/t; 102-Hole Phase Two (TSXV:SGN)
snippet: Scorpio Gold (TSX-V: SGN) reported hole 26MN-099 returning 2.05 g/t Au over 97.99 metres from 64.16m at the Goldwedge Target within the Manhattan property in Nevada's Walker Lane, including high-grade intervals of 18.19 g/t over 3.17m, 11.41 g/t over 4.57m, and 8.98 g/t over 7.32m. The company has now drilled 102 holes totalling 28,939m in its Phase Two program, with the Goldwedge zone's consistent bulk-tonnage widths at moderate-to-high grade supporting a significant open-pittable resource in a Tier 1 US gold district.

headline: TITAN PROVES US GRAPHITE SUPPLY CHAIN — 95.9% Concentrate, 99.9%+ Battery-Grade Purity Achieved; First Fully Integrated US Graphite in 70 Years (TSX:TII)
snippet: Titan Mining (TSX: TII) validated the full processing chain for its Kilbourne Graphite Project, achieving 95.9% concentrate grade at 91.4% recovery, a 66% conversion of concentrate to spherical graphite — well above the industry average of ~50% — and consistent purification to ≥99.90% Fixed Carbon battery grade in testing conducted at Germany's Dorfner Anzaplan. The results advance a feasibility study for what the company is positioning as the first fully integrated US graphite supply chain in over 70 years, targeting domestic battery anode supply for North American EV manufacturers.

headline: US DOE LICENSES SEAWATER URANIUM EXTRACTION — SuperCritical to Commercialize PNNL Ocean Adsorber Tech; 4.5B-Tonne Reserve Now in Commercial Play
snippet: Austin-based SuperCritical Materials secured an exclusive US Department of Energy license to commercialize Pacific Northwest National Laboratory's patented adsorbent technology for extracting uranium and critical materials from seawater, using treated acrylic fibres deployed as ocean arrays. The company cited the world's oceans as containing approximately 4.5 billion tonnes of dissolved uranium — more than 1,000 times known terrestrial reserves — positioning the technology as a long-term uranium supply option as advanced reactor deployments accelerate demand.

headline: USA RARE EARTH EXTRACTS DYSPROSIUM FROM RECYCLED SCRAP — Colorado Hydromet Plant Achieves Commercial Grade Ahead of $2.8B Serra Verde Close (USAR)
snippet: USA Rare Earth successfully produced commercial-grade dysprosium oxide and neodymium-praseodymium oxide samples from recycled rare earth magnet scrap at its Wheat Ridge hydrometallurgical facility in Colorado — a technically demanding separation milestone given dysprosium's chemical complexity. The achievement unlocks a secondary supply stream for critical magnet materials and adds to USA Rare Earth's strategic position ahead of its pending ~US$2.8 billion acquisition of Brazilian primary producer Serra Verde.

headline: GOLD MINERS NEAR SECOND-BEST QUARTER EVER — $2,787/oz Implied Profit at $4,512 Average Gold; GDX P/E Compresses to 20x as Mainstream Ignores
snippet: Adam Hamilton's GoldSeek analysis projects the top-25 GDX gold miners will deliver their second-best quarter ever in Q2 2026, with implied unit profits of approximately $2,787/oz based on an average gold price of ~$4,512 and estimated costs of ~$1,725/oz — a near-50% year-over-year surge in margins. Sector P/E multiples already compressed to 20.2x after Q1 2026 results, a level Hamilton describes as historically unusual given balance sheet strength; Q2 reports beginning in late July could catalyse a rerating while mainstream financial media remains focused on the gold price pullback from $5,595.

headline: JAGUAR TURMALINA POWERS 19% Q2 GOLD JUMP — 13,057 oz, US$74.8M Cash; Full-Year 50K–60K oz Guidance Intact in Brazil (TSX:JAG)
snippet: Jaguar Mining (TSX: JAG) delivered Q2 2026 consolidated production of 13,057 oz Au, up 19% year-over-year, with the newly ramped Turmalina mine contributing 3,994 oz in its first full operating quarter alongside consistent output of 9,063 oz from the flagship Pilar mine in Brazil's Minas Gerais state. The company's cash position strengthened to US$74.8M and full-year guidance of 50,000–60,000 oz was reaffirmed, with Turmalina expected to be a growing contributor in H2 2026.

headline: FRONTIER NUCLEAR LAUNCHES 120-HOLE WYOMING URANIUM DRILL — 36,000m at Pine Ridge Targets ISR Resource in Powder River Basin, Jul–Dec 2026
snippet: Frontier Nuclear and Minerals launched its 2026 drill campaign at the Pine Ridge uranium project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin, targeting approximately 36,000 metres across nearly 120 drill holes scheduled to run from July through December to advance resource definition at this in-situ recovery-style uranium property. The program is one of the largest active uranium drill campaigns in the US and reflects continued operator conviction in Powder River Basin ISR economics as domestic nuclear fuel demand grows ahead of planned advanced reactor commissioning dates.
